resources.content:
## Verification status

Current academic session: 2026/2027. Bowen's academic calendar lists resumption for returning students on 14 September 2026, with registration and lectures beginning in the second week.

### Confirmed from Bowen University material | Area | Evidence | Working status | | --- | --- | --- | | Anatomy | ANA 201 appears in the 2025/2026 College of Health Sciences timetable; ANA 203 also appears | Confirmed | | Physiology | PIO 201 and PIO 208 appear as PHYSIOLOGY courses in the 2025/2026 timetable | Confirmed | | Anatomy practical | ANA 201 LAB and ANA 203 LAB appear in the timetable | Confirmed | | Biochemistry | Bowen timetable evidence shows BCH-labelled teaching associated with the medical/health-science curriculum | Confirmed discipline; exact MBBS 200L code still to verify | | Physiology practical | Bowen timetable evidence shows 200L physiology practical teaching | Confirmed | ## Important correction Do not assume that every PHS/PIO number is a 200L MBBS physiology code. Bowen uses overlapping course-code families across programmes. For example, PIO 201 is explicitly labelled PHYSIOLOGY in the 2025/2026 timetable, while older timetables contain other PHS/PIO codes for different programmes. Therefore the current build uses discipline + verified topic as the content identity until the student's current 2026/2027 course registration/handbook provides the definitive MBBS code list. ## 200L content lanes ### Anatomy - Gross Anatomy - Histology - Embryology - Anatomy practical/dissection ### Physiology - Systems physiology - Physiology practical - Quantitative/graph-based physiology where relevant ### Biochemistry - Molecular biochemistry - Metabolism - Biochemical pathways and clinical correlations ## Production gate Before a topic enters production: 1. Verify it belongs to Bowen 200L. 2. Map it to the student's course/lecture outline. 3. Audit available source material. 4. Identify required visuals. 5. Produce original notes. 6. Generate ≥50 non-duplicative flashcards. 7. Generate ≥50 non-duplicative MCQs. 8. Add 5–6 theory/model-answer questions. 9. Verify calculations and factual claims. 10. Mark the topic complete only after review. ## Current priority Resource audit before content generation. The next task is to identify which 200L Anatomy, Physiology and Biochemistry resources are already available in the connected Drive/workspace, then select the first topic with sufficient source coverage.

## FINAL COURSE RESOURCE ARCHITECTURE The Master Course Map defines where each subtopic belongs. The actual course workspace defines what is attached to it. 200L → Physiology → Topic → Subtopic Each subtopic should be treated as a complete learning unit with these resource layers: - 📖 Notes - ❓ MCQs - 🔄 Flashcards - 📄 Past Papers - 🩺 Clinical Vignettes - 🖼️ Visuals / Diagrams / Graphs - 🧠 Clinical Correlations - 🧪 Practical / Laboratory - ✍️ Theory / SAQs + Model Answers - 📊 Calculations / Data Interpretation where applicable - 🎯 High-Yield / Revision - 📚 Sources / References / Attribution ### Example 200L → Physiology → Topic 4: Cardiovascular Physiology → 4.7 Cardiac Cycle

→ Notes

→ MCQs

→ Flashcards

→ Past Papers

→ Clinical Vignettes

→ Visuals

→ Clinical Correlations

→ Practical

→ Theory / SAQs

→ Calculations / Data Interpretation

→ High-Yield / Revision

→ Sources Rule: Do not create separate disconnected resource systems that lose the Topic/Subtopic relationship. Every resource must remain traceable to its exact 200L course, topic and subtopic. ## INFINITE QUESTION-BANK / RESOURCE-SOURCING STRATEGY ### Core principle After the Notes layer is sufficiently complete, the downstream learning resources should be built from a broad Nigerian medical-education source pool, not from a single university or a single question set. Priority source pool includes publicly available curricula, course outlines, lecture objectives, practical guides, departmental materials and assessment patterns from Nigerian universities. Examples already verified include Bayero University, University of Medical Sciences Ondo, Federal University Oye-Ekiti, Olabisi Onabanjo University, State University of Medical and Applied Sciences, and other Nigerian institutions where relevant. ### Question-bank objective Build an extremely large, high-quality question bank so that the learner—not the content author—controls the size of each study session. The app should eventually support: - User-selected number of questions - Topic/subtopic filtering - Course filtering - Difficulty filtering - Question-type filtering - Randomized selection - No-repeat exposure until the available pool has been exhausted, where technically feasible - Persistent question history so previously seen questions can be tracked - Multiple attempts without recycling the same questions unnecessarily - Weak-area targeting - Fresh mixed-question sessions - Progressive difficulty ### Source integrity Do NOT copy large blocks of copyrighted university examination papers or lecture materials verbatim. Use legitimate/publicly available material to identify tested concepts, learning objectives, question styles and curriculum coverage, then create original, academically equivalent questions and explanations. Past-paper questions may be linked/referenced where legitimately available, but the internal generated bank should be original, transformed and traceable to its learning objective/source concept. ### Resource layers after Notes For each relevant subtopic, progressively build: Notes → Visuals → Clinical Correlations/Vignettes → Flashcards → MCQs → Past Papers → Theory/SAQs → Practical/Data Interpretation → High-Yield Revision Not every layer must exist identically for every subtopic; use academic judgment. For example, quantitative physiology should receive substantially more calculations/data interpretation, while anatomy should receive substantially more labelled visuals/practical identification. ### Nigerian-source diversity The goal is not to imitate one university. Cross-check Nigerian curricula and teaching emphasis to identify: - Commonly taught concepts - University-specific emphasis - Recurring examination themes - Practical competencies - Terminology differences - Areas commonly tested across institutions Then synthesize these into a broader TheMedConfidant bank. ### Current verification examples Bayero University's published MBBS/BDS physiology structure includes General Principles and Cell Physiology, Excitable Tissues, Autonomic Nervous System, Blood and Immunity, Cardiovascular System, practical physiology, then Respiratory, Renal, Metabolism/Skin, Gastrointestinal, Liver/Biliary, Endocrine and Reproductive physiology. citeturn0search0turn0search3 UNIMED's 200L MBBS structure includes Gross Anatomy, Histology, Embryology, General Biochemistry, Introductory/General Physiology, Blood and Body Fluid, Excitable Tissue/Contractile Cells/CNS/ANS, then GI, Respiratory and Cardiovascular Physiology. citeturn0search1 FUOYE and other Nigerian institutions similarly show 200L physiology alongside anatomy and biochemistry, reinforcing the need for a cross-university rather than single-school architecture. citeturn0search11turn0search9 This source-diversity rule applies to the whole 200L build, not just Physiology. ## 200L PHYSIOLOGY — NORMALIZED CURRICULUM MAP (WORKING MASTER) ### TOPIC 1 — General → Clinical Correlations → Clinical Vignettes → Flashcards → MCQs → Past Papers → Theory/SAQs → Practical/Laboratory → Calculations/Data Interpretation → High-Yield/Revision → Sources/Attribution. ## LEGACY MIGRATION RULE Existing flat-numbered pages (including the previously built 1–118+ and later extension pages) are source material, not final numbering. They must be mapped into the normalized Topic/Subtopic structure and retained; do not delete or duplicate them unnecessarily. Where an existing page combines multiple concepts, split its content conceptually across the relevant subtopics rather than forcing the old number into the new system. ## QUESTION-BANK PRINCIPLE After notes are stable, assessment resources should be sourced/triangulated against Bowen first, then broader Nigerian university curricula and assessment patterns. Genuine past-paper material must remain clearly identified as such; original questions should be generated from the verified learning objectives and assessment patterns. The eventual bank should be deliberately very large so the learner can select a session size while the engine minimizes unnecessary repetition. ## 🔥 CURRENT BUILD STATUS — 30 AUG 2026 Strategy: Bowen-first preclinical build. Existing legacy physiology material is being reorganized into the new Topic → Subtopic architecture; no unnecessary rewriting. ### Production pipeline Curriculum audit → Notes → Visuals → Clinical correlations/vignettes → Flashcards → Massive MCQ bank → Past papers → Theory/SAQs → Practical/data interpretation → High-yield/revision → QA ### Assessment-bank principle The question bank is intentionally vast, not capped at an arbitrary number per subtopic. Questions will be sourced/derived from Bowen assessment patterns first, then triangulated against Nigerian university curricula and publicly available educational/assessment material. Genuine past-paper questions remain clearly identified; original questions are generated from the same tested concepts rather than misrepresented as past papers. ### Anti-repeat objective The eventual quiz engine should draw from the largest feasible pool, track questions already served to the learner, minimize repeats, and allow the learner to choose a session size/topic/difficulty. Repetition should be used deliberately for weak-area reinforcement, not because the bank is small. ### Scope discipline Current scope is preclinical 100L + 200L. Multi-university support is a later mapping layer; 300L+ and clinical-year content are not current production targets. ### Architecture target 200L → Course → Topic → Subtopic → resource ecosystem Every course should have its own resource hubs (Notes, MCQs, Flashcards, Past Papers, etc.), while each subtopic remains traceable to its exact course/topic/subtopic. ## CLEANUP STATUS — 30 AUG 2026 Active navigation uses the final hierarchy: 200L → Physiology → Topic → Subtopic. Legacy numbered pages are source/archive material only and must not appear as active navigation entries.
